# Qualification test output and release status

**Bottom line:** Qualification evidence is generated by each test run. It is
not stored in the source tree. The result qualifies the function only for the
experimental Linux image-file scope. It does not qualify direct use on user
volumes. The normal build does not build or install the defragmenter.

The test build uses exfat-next commit
`1647ed54299ae8c4343a5edf40b892307f7e6459` as its historical baseline. Each
run records the compiler, platform, source hashes, binary build options, test
results, and logs in its output directory. `manifest.json` contains a SHA-256
digest for every other regular output file.

## Test program and output

| Test | Qualification criterion | Output in a full run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nine focused historical regressions | Each case reproduces the expected defect on the pinned baseline and passes on the repaired worker | `baseline/results.json`, `regressions/results.json`, `sanitizer-regressions/results.json` |
| Native model | 1,000 seeds with 5,000 iterations plus two capacity cases; each valid fragmented image finishes with zero discontinuities | `model/results.json`, `model/cases.jsonl` |
| ASan, UBSan, and leak-detection model | The same model cases pass without a sanitizer diagnostic | `sanitizer-model/results.json`, `sanitizer-model/cases.jsonl` |
| Geometry, vendor, occupancy, and depth matrix | All selected combinations pass for native and sanitizer builds | `matrix/results.json`, `sanitizer-matrix/results.json` |
| Linux exFAT driver | Ten seeds complete the driver workload, offline defrag, remount, and model comparison | `driver/results.json`, when `--driver` is selected |
| Small-fixture fault matrix | Every planned worker write position and host boundary is reached and has the required recovery result | `faults/results.json`, `faults/cases.jsonl`, `faults/host-boundaries.json`, `faults/worker-boundaries.json`, and sanitizer equivalents |
| Explicit persistence model | Prefix loss, reordering, and half writes recover the exact original bytes | `persistence/results.json`, `persistence/cases.jsonl`, and sanitizer equivalents |
| Copy and publication | The source stays unchanged; invalid output is not published; no-replace and post-link errors have the documented result | `publication/results.json` and `sanitizer-publication/results.json` |
| Negative checks | Invalid layouts, containers, ownership, links, and lock conflicts are rejected without changing the complete source | `negative/results.json` and `sanitizer-negative/results.json` |
| Metadata and boot bytes | Attributes, times, subseconds, UTC offsets, VDL, and unrelated boot bytes stay equal | `metadata/results.json` and `sanitizer-metadata/results.json` |
| Directory flush and host death | Flush errors propagate; undo restores exact bytes; invalid journals and a dead host cannot leave a competing worker | `transaction_regressions/results.json` and `sanitizer-transaction_regressions/results.json` |
| Existing upstream corruption fixtures | Detect, repair, and clean reread pass for every selected fixture | `upstream/results.json` and `sanitizer-upstream/results.json` |

The main native and sanitizer model runs use the same seeds. They are not two
independent seed sets. Model iterations are not Linux file-system calls. The
matrix is separate from the model seed count. A baseline PASS means that the
test reproduced the old defect. It does not mean that the old implementation
is correct.

## Run and inspect qualification

Run a short qualification before review and a full qualification before a
release claim:

```sh
python3 tests/defrag/qualify.py --out defrag-test-results-smoke
python3 tests/defrag/qualify.py --full --driver --jobs 4 \
  --out defrag-test-results-full
```

Use a new output directory for every run. The top-level `results.json` reports
each invoked step and its status. `PASS_WITH_BLOCKERS` means that at least one
required capability, such as the optional driver run, was NOT_RUN. NOT_RUN is
not PASS and cannot support the related release claim.

The `Experimental defrag qualification` GitHub Actions workflow uploads each
output directory as a job artifact. Pushes and pull requests produce GCC,
Clang, and focused sanitizer artifacts. The scheduled full job produces the
complete rootless artifact. A manual workflow run can also produce the
privileged Linux-driver artifact. CI artifacts are retained temporarily; save
an artifact outside GitHub before its retention period ends if it must become a
long-lived release record.

For fault injection with ASan, `DEFRAG_ASAN_RUNTIME` is the result of
`cc -print-file-name=libasan.so`. This loads the ASan runtime before the worker
interposer. Python and fsck do not use that interposer.

## Evidence limits

The test program does not include a big-endian hardware run, hardware power
loss, large-volume defrag, TexFAT defrag, general vendor defrag, or bad-cluster
defrag. The persistence model is separate from a real device power-loss test.
A successful run does not remove the release limits in
[ADR 0004](adr/0004-release.md).

A raw-worker I/O error can leave an inconsistent image. The raw-worker tests
check error propagation. Separate journal tests check exact safe recovery. This
is why a local worker repair or a copy wrapper alone is not sufficient.
